Our NFL Player Prop Bet Cheat Sheet assists bettors by comparing lines from leading sportsbooks with our daily NFL projections. What is an NFL player prop bet? An NFL player prop bet is a type of wager where you’re betting on the performance of a specific player in a game rather than the overall outcome. For example, you might place a bet on how many passing yards a quarterback will throw for, or how many touchdowns a running back will score. It’s a fun way to get more invested in the action, especially if you’re confident in how a particular player will perform, regardless of who wins or loses the game. It’s like focusing on one slice of the pie instead of the whole thing. Whether you're new to sports betting or a betting pro, our Sports Betting Strategy and Advice page is for you.

The Vikings love to pressure the quarterback, and their blitz and pressure rates are among the highest in NFL history. One way to combat that pressure is to get the running back out of the backfield quickly and find him on mismatches. We saw it last week when McCaffrey got matched up on Von Miller for a touchdown. I think the 49ers have to use McCaffrey in the passing game to have success against Minnesota's pressure. I like the Over on his receptions. This line could reflect Tampa Bay possibly being without quarterback Baker Mayfield, who is questionable with multiple injuries. However, I believe Mayfield will play, with the Bucs still in the hunt for a division title. He's a tough guy, and he won't miss this game. Even still, I'd still take the Bucs with Jalon Daniels under center. This number is too big. Detroit's defense is without its two best players: Jack Campbell is unavailable, and star pass rusher Aidan Hutchinson was injured last week.

The Lions' pass rush is significantly worse without Hutchinson, and any team, including the Bucs, will take advantage of it. No Lions lead will be safe moving forward. Tampa Bay has the weapons to score on this defense, and I believe it will. On the other side, there is Detroit's fantastic offense. It's a legitimately good group. However, the Bucs are first in the NFL in defensive EPA per play, even ahead of the Vikings, and they're good at stopping both the run and the pass. They haven't faced an offense quite like the Lions yet, but their defensive production has still been excellent. I believe Tampa Bay's defense can slow down the Lions enough to cover.

results.title: 2026 NFL Week 12 Best Bets, Expert Picks: Back Chiefs, Josh Allen On Thanksgiving
results.description: Geoff Schwartz likes Kansas City as a road underdog in Buffalo and has a Josh Allen rushing prop for Thanksgiving night.
highlights: 2026 NFL Week 12 Best Bets, Expert Picks: Back Chiefs, Josh Allen On Thanksgiving The Chiefs and Bills meet on Thanksgiving night, and I'm getting Patrick Mahomes with a field goal? I'm thankful. Here is how I'm wagering the holiday weekend in the professional football ranks. This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX Sports may be compensated. Read more about Sports Betting on FOX Sports. Again, Patrick Mahomes getting a field goal in a regular-season game? Sign me up. The Chiefs' offense has been playing its best football in years over the last month. I understand the competition hasn't been great, but great teams should beat the heck out of bad defenses. Kansas City finally has a wide receiver corps good enough for a complete passing game. The Chiefs might also have the best running back duo in the NFL, which will continue to matter as Kenneth Walker III works through a lower-leg injury.

Both passing games could suffer in the wind and rain, which makes running the ball even more important. Geoff Schwartz Schwartz's Pick: Josh Allen Over 40 rushing yards Lastly, I'm taking the Chiefs to cover. It worries me a bit that Kansas City can't seem to win or cover against Buffalo in the regular season. It feels like the Chiefs hold some things back against the Bills, knowing they'll likely see them again in the postseason. But this is the best the Chiefs have played entering a Bills game in years, and I believe they want to win this one. They're also starting a brutal stretch of games that will define their season, and they need to start it with a win. Geoff Schwartz Schwartz's Pick: Chiefs +3

I do worry about the Chiefs' offensive line against the Bills' defensive line. That's an advantage for Buffalo, but I trust Mahomes and Andy Reid to have a plan to navigate it. The Chiefs' defense has been great, but it hasn't played an offense like the Bills, which is multidimensional with quarterback Josh Allen and running back James Cook. That said, Allen hasn't played like an MVP. He's seventh in EPA per play but only 14th in completion percentage, with 14 touchdown passes and nine interceptions. He adds plenty with his legs, which is what makes him such a dangerous quarterback, and that's where I look first for a wager in this game. I love taking Allen's rushing yards Over in monster Bills games. This is where his legs are such an advantage: third-down rushing attempts and late scrambles for yards. Allen has crushed the Chiefs with his legs over the years, and I'll keep believing in that here. The weather might also be a factor.

highlights: Value is value, no matter where -- or how -- you find it. And that's what we'll aim to do each week in this space: finding betting value. Ben Solak, Seth Walder and Matt Bowen bring different perspectives into how they approach sports betting. Solak leans on his expertise in player evaluation and the X's and O's to find edges, while Walder relies on statistical models to pick out plus-expected value bets, focusing mainly on defense. From spreads and money lines to totals and defensive player props, a good price might be found anywhere. Results will be tracked throughout the season, with flat one-unit wagers for each listed bet. With that, let's dive into our best bets, favorite defensive props and the top game to bet in Week 3. I tend to stay away from double-digit spreads in this league (especially for road favorites).

The Bucs have had Robinson on the field on just 23% of clear pass rushing situations this season, down from 52% last year in Carolina. Other sack bets I recommend: Jaelan Phillips UNDER 0.75 sacks (+125) Leonard Williams UNDER 0.25 sacks (-109) Chris Jones UNDER 0.25 sacks (-138) Andrew Van Ginkel UNDER 0.25 sacks (-128) Donovan Ezeiruaku UNDER 4.5 tackles + assists (-107) Ezeiruaku has been playing a little more this season -- 65% of snaps this year vs. 55% last year -- but that's not nearly enough to overcome this high line for an edge rusher. I think what's happening here is this line is being inflated by an outlandish 10-tackle game in Week 1. But it was only the third time Ezeiruaku had ever gone over 4.5 combined tackles in his career.

If Ezeiruaku's role had changed substantially in addition to the slight uptick in playing time this would be a different story, but he's still playing as a 7 or 9 technique 93% of the time (was 89% last year). And Ezeiruaku's tackle rate was almost exactly average for an edge rusher last year. I think the under here is an excellent value. Jordyn Brooks UNDER 9.5 tackles + assists (-116) It's pretty easy to imagine how Brooks could accrue a gaudy tackle number in this game. The Chiefs are double-digit favorites, have been having success with the ground game and if they get out to a big lead they'll simply run the ball to run out the clock. The result? Plenty of tackle opportunities for Miami's defense, and in particular a linebacker like Brooks. But the model knows all that and says this line is just far too high. Just last week Miami was massive underdogs to the 49ers and Brooks recorded just three combined tackles. I would bet this down to -150.
